title: Validity of a certificate string
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, and let $n,s$ be natural numbers and $w$ a finite Boolean string. The string is valid exactly when its length is $W(N)(2s+1)+wP(n)+1$, the scan of its prefix of length $W(N)(2s+1)$ is accepting, the binary value of the next $wP(n)$ bits is at most $n+1$, and the bit at index $W(N)(2s+1)+wP(n)$ is true (with out-of-range lookup interpreted as false).
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the meanings of $W(N)$, $wP(n)$, or the binary-value function, so these quantities can only be named descriptively.
